summary: Season 1 (our eps 1-52) adapts Hayate no Gotoku! in a deliberately SHUFFLED order rather than a linear run: eps 1-3 take ch 1-7, then ep 4 jumps to v4 ch 34-36, ep 5 returns to ch 11/16, and the season keeps criss-crossing the manga for the rest of its run, with late grafts from v7-v12 (ch 65, 68-71, 73, 85, 90, 99-104, 107, 128, 129) dropped into episodes that otherwise sit in v2-v5. 30 anchors are produced across eps 1-49. Two target episodes get no anchor: ep 10 is anime-only (type correction proposed) and the ep 52 finale adapts only the volume-4 and volume-8 BONUS chapters ('Radical Dreamers', 'Small Two of Pieces'), which have no mainline chapter number — an honest gap rather than an invented END. Because the adaptation order is non-monotonic, the END chapters do NOT increase with episode number (…36, 16, 20, 23, 19, 46, …, 68, 48, 25, 85, 70, 28, 32, 99, 71, 65, 129, 51, 100, 103, 128), so any interpolating position model must be suppressed for eps 1-52; the honest reader resume for the whole season is ch 52, which is exactly where season 2 (our ep 53) picks up. Row identity was verified against ja.wikipedia and en.wikipedia by air date and Japanese title at eps 1/20/29/52 — no Ryuusui-class numbering shift exists here.

continue_points.note: Season-1 finale adapts only bonus chapters, so there is no END+1. Season 2 (our ep 53) begins at ch 52, and ch 52 is also the first mainline chapter S1 never touched in a continuous run — so 52 is the honest resume after finishing S1. Chapters 9, 24, 29 and 33 are skipped by S1 and are never adapted by any season.

type_corrections.note: Stored as canon, but ep 10 adapts no manga: English Wikipedia's episode list states outright 'This episode, which is anime-only', the fandom episode page is the only S1 canon-numbered page with NO 'Adapted From' section, and no chapter page in the whole 1-140 sweep names ep 10. Story (Abe Maou inside a Famicom game) and its characters have no manga counterpart. NB: fandom trivia says the episode was 'originally drafted by Kenjiro Hata', which would argue for anime-only-canon instead — flagged for Sean; either way A1 forbids an anchor.

Stored as filler, but ep 19 adapts ch 49: the episode's Japanese title サキさんのヤボ用(全国版)2007 is ch 49's title サキさんのヤボ用(全国版) verbatim plus a year, the Saki coming-of-age/kimono plot is ch 49's plot, the fandom episode page credits ch 49 + a volume-3 omake, and ch 49's own page names ep 19. The cursed-video/giant-cockroach B-plot is anime-original, hence mixed rather than canon. NO ANCHOR REQUESTED — out of the gap scope and A1 applies until the type is changed.

structure.notes: ROW-COUNT IDENTITY (Ryuusui-class check): CLEAN for eps 1-52. Fandom episode pages 1-52 carry ep= and date= fields that match en.wikipedia's episode list and ja.wikipedia's 各話リスト one-for-one at every point checked (ep 1 = 2007-04-01, ep 20 = 2007-08-12, ep 29 = 2007-10-14, ep 52 = 2008-03-30), and those match our stored air dates exactly. No source inserts the OVA or the movie into the TV numbering, so there is no shift. OPEN FLAG #829 RESOLVED for this range: the 29 title conflicts are translation variance, not an offset — e.g. our 'A New Beginning with Nagi Sanzenin's Estate' vs the wiki's 'Nagi Sanzenin's Mansion and a New Journey' (both 三千院ナギの屋敷と、新たなる旅立ち), 'Match-Making Meeting' vs 'Marriage Meeting' (見合). Stored titles should be kept. OPEN FLAG #672: the reading edition is the 1-513 mainline chapter numbering used by both en.wikipedia's chapter list and the fandom wiki, which reproduces the stored volume boundaries exactly (v1 1-9, v4 32-41, v8 75-85, v10 97-107, v12 119-129, v47 503-513). AniList's 570 and MU's 305 are both other counts; anchors here are in the 1-513 space. EPISODE-ROW GAP: the context file lists only 54 rows for a 101-episode series — eps 1-52, 77 and 101. Eps 53-76 and 78-100 appear to have no rows at all, which is why only 32 of the 100 target episodes were anchorable. Worth a separate row-ingest pass. SEASON BOUNDARY: season 2 (our ep 53) starts at ch 52 (fandom ch 52 page names 'Hayate no Gotoku!! Episode 1'), so S1 ends without ever adapting ch 9, 24, 29 or 33 — those four are never adapted by any season.

flags_for_sean: POSITION MODEL: season 1's END chapters are strongly non-monotonic (ep 4 = 36, ep 5 = 16; ep 22 = 85, ep 23 = 70; ep 42 = 129, ep 43 = 51). Interpolating between these anchors will produce nonsense. Recommend the rearranged annotation gate any interpolation over eps 1-52 and that per-episode continue points be suppressed for the season — the only continue point I could defend is ep 52 -> ch 52.

ep 52 has NO anchor by design: the finale adapts only the volume-4 and volume-8 BONUS chapters. Protocol forbids converting those to mainline numbers, so the season boundary anchor is an honest gap. If a boundary anchor is required for the UI, it should be recorded as a continue point (52), not a fabricated end_chapter.

ep 10 type: proposed filler, but the fandom page's trivia says the story was 'originally drafted by Kenjiro Hata' (stated in-episode by the narrator/Maria, so possibly a gag). If that credit is real the correct type is anime-only-canon. Either way it takes no anchor.

Three more stored-filler rows carry fandom chapter credits I did NOT correct because the evidence is fandom-only (forward + reverse pages, no independent corroboration): ep 35 -> ch 107 'A Lonesome War', ep 37 -> ch 73 'Heart To Heart' (ch 73 is ALSO credited to Hayate no Gotoku!! ep 5, which is likely the real adaptation), ep 41 -> ch 101 'You Don't Have Enough Kung Fu'. If Sean wants them re-typed mixed, they need a third source first.

Six anchors are medium (eps 12, 17, 23, 42, 47, 49): in each the END chapter's fandom page is a Summary stub, so the END rests on the fandom episode page + fandom chapter page pair without independent content confirmation. The START chapter of each of those is independently corroborated.

ep 17 END: fandom credits ch 68 AND ch 100. I set END = 68 and demoted ch 100 to an annotation because ep 44 is the full ch 100 adaptation and ep 17 uses only the Britney manga cold open. If Sean prefers the literal running-order rule, END would be 100 — but that would put ep 17 ahead of ep 44 in position.
